claims.text: Tobias Renn has kept the Grey Point lighthouse for 32 years and logs every ship that crosses the bar.
The Grey Point Trust voted in March to keep the old lamp, by 42 votes to nine.
Renn says an electric lamp would have cost the Trust 150 thousand dollars before a single night of light.
His ledger showed 64 ships turning back at the bar last winter, twice the year before.
The Harbour Board sets the dredging budget every spring from its own count, which is lower than his.
The apprentices are paid from visitor tickets and a small grant from the county.

headline: Read the [ledger](ledger) before the vote.
new: The Trust's March vote settled the lamp for now; the county's visitor-centre plan is still open.

quotes.speaker: Tobias Renn
quotes.text: Because the dredging budget follows the count, and the Harbour Board sets the dredging budget every spring.

title: Who counts the ships at Grey Point?
